answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with stake-backed attestation shaped like a trellis. Each agent locks a refundable bond to one identity, so forging a thousand fakes costs a thousand bonds. Peers vouch only for counterparts they have worked with, and these vouches interlock like a trellis, so a fake cluster with few links stands out. A regular pulse of verifiable work keeps an identity alive, while copied answers or fake vouches slash the bond and remove the cluster. Forging reputation becomes expensive, because one operator cannot cheaply forge the history many peers must confirm.
